title: Catalog curation and runway gating: version pinning & retirement prioritization for enterprise model requests
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers increasingly request: (a) pinning to specific model commits for regulatory reproducibility, (b) explicit deprecation timelines for models used in workflows, and (c) expedited onboarding of commercial/open models with contractual SLAs. Current catalog flows do not surface a consistent severity/prioritization for these requests, which leads to ad-hoc pinning, surprise regressions, and emergency rollouts.

Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable curation & runway gating process that: 1) scores incoming enterprise model requests, 2) defines version-pin windows and auto-retirement trigger criteria, 3) introduces an "expedited enterprise lane" with minimal guardrails (eval gate checklist + contract flag), and 4) produces operational artifacts (pin records, deprecation notices, and rollout plans) that integrate with Console and the model catalog UI.

Scope: Non-bug product work for model catalog change requests only (new model adds, pin requests, planned deprecations). Not in scope: runtime kernel changes, infra capacity procurement, or ad-hoc model hotfixes.

Success metrics: median time-to-decision for enterprise model requests <= 5 business days; reduction in emergency rollback incidents due to uncommunicated deprecations by 80% in two quarters; surveyed enterprise customers report "predictable model lifecycle" satisfaction >= 4/5.

Constraints & trade-offs considered:
- Manual review vs. automated score: initial rollout will be semi-automated (scoring matrix + PM review) to avoid false negatives on safety/contract flags.
- Strict pinning window length: longer windows increase reproducibility but raise operational cost; propose tiered defaults (90d standard, 180d enterprise SLA) with opt-outs.
- Eval gate strictness: will balance false-positives (blocking useful models) with customer trust. We will start with an eval checklist (latency, mem, hallucination spot-checks, licensing check) and iterate using telemetry.

Deliverables: scoring rubric doc, pin/retirement policy, Confluence runbook for PMs/SEs, a draft UI wireframe for Console annotations, and an automation GH issue to create pin records from accepted requests.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible scoring rubric (CSV + Confluence page) that yields a numeric priority for new model requests and pin/retire requests.
Policy document specifying default pin windows, enterprise SLA pin window overrides, and explicit retirement triggers (usage threshold, security/OSS licensing change, model-quality regression).
Runbook for PM/SE handling of an "expedited enterprise lane" with a required eval gate checklist and required signoffs listed.
Mockups in Drive for Console annotations that surface pin status, retirement ETA, and links to evaluation artifacts (link included below).
Automation GH issue created (ENG backlog) to wire accepted requests into the catalog metadata and emit deprecation notifications at t-minus milestones.
